segments.heading: One line per run file: checksum, then file name
segments.text:
Checksum that `go.sh`, the driver script of the rerun, had at launch.
- Every line has the same format: the sha256 of the file content as 64 hexadecimal digits, then two spaces, then the file name. This is the output format of the tool `sha256sum`.
- The local go.sh no longer has this checksum. Its line 20 was edited on 2026-11-24 (the text of one message). Its sha256 is now d68cf6c0468abeb658765b950b9bd86b34ff9556070efcd954824f6e936da2bd. With the old line 20 put back it has the listed value again [Ref8].
- The facts sheet states that the 2 logs, the 3 probe.txt files and the 9 env.txt files of the rerun hold no sha256 of go.sh [Ref3].
- The session record holds a test of the copy on CRB. The command that copied the five files of this list to CRB ran `sha256sum -c local.sha` there. It printed `go.sh: OK` about 5 s before go.sh was started [Ref7].

Checksum of `ra.sh`, the script of part A. ra.sh also writes its own sha256 into `probe.txt` on CRB [Ref5]. The 3 probe.txt files of part A hold this same value (check 18 of the facts sheet) [Ref6] [Ref3].

Checksums of the three spec files:
- `like.spec`: the argument line of part L and of control I.
- `cfwd.spec`: the argument line of part C in the order oldread, read, asmread.
- `crev.spec`: the argument line of part C in the order asmread, read, oldread.
No script of the rerun computes a checksum of a spec file on CRB. The facts sheet compares the launch lines that rx.sh wrote on CRB with the text of the three files (check 15) [Ref1]. The command that copied the files to CRB tested the three copies there against this list. It printed `OK` for each [Ref7].
